headline: In-house software; referred to the business head, but 'please don't use my name'

suggested_routes.label: Deal / partner next step
suggested_routes.rationale: A cold referral to the business head via a networking site, with an explicit constraint on using the contact's name.
suggested_routes.evidence_ref: C09 — "No, please don't use my name."
suggested_routes.output: Next step: approach Mr Rishabh (business head) through the professional networking site without mentioning Vedant. Lead with the open question of whether the in-house system executes payments or only records them.

suggested_routes.label: Sales coaching
suggested_routes.rationale: Good practice: the rep asked permission before using the contact's name and respected the refusal.
suggested_routes.evidence_ref: C09 — "Would it be all right if I mentioned your name when contacting him?"
suggested_routes.output: Reinforce: ask before using a referrer's name, as Meera did here. The answer changes how the next touch is written.

evidence.quote: We have developed our own software internally, so at present we aren't looking for anything outside the organisation.
evidence.supports: The prospect has no current need.

evidence.quote: you can find our business head, Mr Rishabh, on a professional networking site.

concise_output: A 130-location business uses internally built software and is not looking externally. Vedant pointed Meera to the business head, Mr Rishabh, but asked not to be named.
what_established: In-house system; Vedant does not know whether it executes payments; business head named; name use refused.
what_not_established: Any gap in the in-house software or interest from the business head.
next_action: Approach the business head without referencing Vedant.
uncertainty: Referral to a cold contact; low likelihood of near-term need.
